title: Character, Calling & Conviction
audience: Pastors and missionaries · opening overview, first of four speakers
bigIdea: His power isn't about how we change ourselves. It's about what He makes us into.

keyPoints: [@8xceteq6] ...And then[Acts 1:8]

[@8xceteq6][Acts 1:8]Acts 1:  8 - But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; 

That next phrase brought even more excitement:  I am sure they thought... "Awesome!! We get power!!!",  but little did they know what lay ahead. Although it was full of power, it was also full of trials, hard times, persecutions and even death.

If I want to experience the Power of God in my life I should expect nothing different. His power, but in the midst of difficulties, hard times and struggles.
"You shall receive power" will bring opposition.
"You shall receive power" will bring difficulties.
"You shall receive power" will bring hard times.
"You shall receive power" will bring jail.
"You shall receive power" will bring conflict.
"You shall receive power" will bring thorns in the flesh.
"You shall receive power" WILL reveal our weakness.

But then...

In our weakness He is strong.
In our weakness He works in mighty ways.
In our weakness He brings healing.
In our weakness He saves people.
In our weakness He brings revival.
In our weakness He transforms us.
In our weakness He changes the world.

Don't expect "you shall receive power" will look any different in your life than it did for the disciples.

verses.text: They called the apostles in and had them flogged. Then they ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go. The apostles left the Sanhedrin, rejoicing because they had been counted worthy of suffering disgrace for the Name.

But the Lord said to Ananias, "Go! This man is my chosen instrument to proclaim my name to the Gentiles and their kings and to the people of Israel. I will show him how much he must suffer for my name."

points.script:
[@xqaxyjrq] And look at what happened next. Within a few chapters, Peter and John are in jail. Then all the apostles are arrested, flogged, and ordered never to speak in the name of Jesus again. 
[@xqax8ejy]
Stephen is stoned. James is killed with a sword. The church is scattered. They expected a throne. They got a road.

And when Jesus calls Paul, He tells Ananias, "This man is my chosen instrument." And in the same breath: "I will show him how much he must suffer for my name." The calling and the suffering came in the same sentence.

The word Jesus used for witness is martys, the word we get martyr from. When He said, "You will be my witnesses," they had no idea yet what that word would come to mean.

The disciples received power, and it brought prison, conflict and weakness.

So don't expect it to look any different for you. I think a lot of us in ministry carry a quiet expectation. If I'm really called, if God's power is really on me, things should go well. The church should grow. The money should come in. The board should agree with me. And when it doesn't, we wonder what we did wrong.

Maybe nothing. Maybe that's just what the power looks like.

sections.title: What the power makes us into

points.slideTitle: His power isn't about how we change ourselves.
points.slide: It's about what He makes us into.
keyPoints: [@whn7dfkn] We argue about what the power looks like
[@whn7cid2] Miracles vs. "God doesn't work that way now"
[@whn7kj1g] Not arguing today
[@whn7gtmw] Wrong question: what it does
[@whn7ncep] Jesus: what it makes them into ("you will BE")
[@whn7z0qm] Potter: marred pot, formed into another
[@whn8c9kh] 🔑 "His power isn't about how we change ourselves. It's about what He makes us into."

verses.text: But the pot he was shaping from the clay was marred in his hands; so the potter formed it into another pot, shaping it as seemed best to him.

points.script:
Now, we can argue a lot about what that power is supposed to look like and what it is supposed to do. Some of us say the power is about miracles and healing and signs. Some of us say God doesn't really work that way anymore. And we could spend this whole conference arguing about it.

I don't want to argue today. I want to suggest that maybe we're asking the wrong question. We keep asking what the power does. Jesus was describing what the power would make them into. He didn't say, "You will do witnessing." He said, "You will be my witnesses."

Jeremiah went down to the potter's house and watched him work. The pot was marred in his hands. So the potter didn't throw the clay away. He formed it into another pot, shaping it as seemed best to him.

His power isn't about how we change ourselves. It's about what He makes us into.

keyPoints: Acts 1:8 power = dynamis
Same word: 2 Cor 12:9
We love "dynamite"
Paul begged 3x for the thorn to go
God said no: power made perfect in weakness
"When I am weak, then I am strong"

verses.text: But he said to me, "My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness." Therefore I will boast all the more gladly about my weaknesses, so that Christ's power may rest on me. That is why, for Christ's sake, I delight in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions, in difficulties. For when I am weak, then I am strong.

points.script:
The word Jesus uses for power in Acts 1:8 is dynamis. And it is the same word Paul uses in 2 Corinthians 12:9, when the Lord tells him, "My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness."

Same word. Same power.

We get our word dynamite from it, and we love that. We want the dynamite. But look where Paul found it. He had begged God three times to take his thorn away, and God said no. So Paul says, "I will boast all the more gladly about my weaknesses, so that Christ's power may rest on me... For when I am weak, then I am strong."

keyPoints: Peter the strong one: first to speak, out of the boat, the sword
The ear: strength without character
"Even if all fall away, I never will"
Real conviction, but his own
Failed by a fire, a servant girl
Me as a dad: my conviction in them washed away
Conviction must be planted inside
The look, wept bitterly
Second fire: breakfast on the beach
Three denials, three questions: "Feed my sheep"
Had to break his self-sufficiency

verses.text: Peter declared, "Even if all fall away, I will not." "Truly I tell you," Jesus answered, "today, yes, tonight, before the rooster crows twice you yourself will disown me three times." But Peter insisted emphatically, "Even if I have to die with you, I will never disown you." And all the others said the same.
When they had finished eating, Jesus said to Simon Peter, "Simon son of John, do you love me more than these?" "Yes, Lord," he said, "you know that I love you." Jesus said, "Feed my lambs."

points.script:
Go back to Peter. Peter was the strong one. He was the first to speak, the first to step out of the boat, the first to pull out a sword in the garden. He cut off a man's ear. That was strength without character.

Peter was the one who said, "Even if all fall away, I will not." That was his conviction. And he meant it. But it was his conviction, not God's. And it failed him by a fire, in front of a servant girl.

I learned this one as a dad. I could be a pretty legalistic father. I was focused on my kids' behavior, not what was going on in their hearts. And as they grew up, a lot of those behaviors just washed away. Because it was my conviction in them. It was never their own. Conviction that is put on you from the outside doesn't hold. It has to be planted on the inside.

Luke tells us that the Lord turned and looked straight at Peter, and Peter went outside and wept bitterly. That night by the fire, something in Peter broke. And it had to.

Then a few weeks later, there's another fire. Jesus makes breakfast on the beach. Three denials, and now three questions: "Peter, do you love me?" "Feed my sheep." The calling comes back, but this time it isn't resting on Peter's strength.

Before God could use Peter, He had to break Peter's self-sufficiency. I believe God cannot use someone who is not broken.

points.slide: We spend our whole lives striving to be strong, when God is calling us to be weak.
keyPoints: Hard part for leaders
We got here by being strong
Have the answer, fix the problem
"Nobody sends a weak missionary"
Me: 30 years in business, the one they called when things broke
Watchman Nee: "Effort is not the key to maturity; death is."
🔑 "We spend our whole lives striving to be strong, when God is calling us to be weak."
points.script:
And this is the hard part for us as leaders. Most of us got where we are because we were strong. We were the ones who could handle it. People look to us. We have to have the answer, preach the sermon, fix the problem, keep the ministry going. Nobody hires a weak pastor. Nobody sends out a weak missionary.

I know this one personally. I spent about thirty years in business, and I was the one they called when things broke. Being strong was my job.

Watchman Nee said, "Effort is not the key to maturity; death is." That is not the kind of thing you put on a leadership poster.

We spend our whole lives striving to be strong, when God is calling us to be weak.

keyPoints: Dad, Gene: ~30 yrs Navigators in PH
Effort focused: "It's you, it's you"
Left the field broken
Construction supervisor for my uncle
Changed with age: never about his effort
2009: hospital at St. Luke's, saw his old disciples still serving
"We sow, we water... God makes it grow"
His "faulty ministry model" → "He is enough!"
Discipled two young men when I was three
Today: our school director and our pastor, ~20 yrs
Thought it came to nothing. God wasn't done.

verses.text: I planted the seed, Apollos watered it, but God has been making it grow. So neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything, but only God, who makes things grow.

points.script:
My dad, Gene Denler, was a missionary here in the Philippines for about thirty years with the Navigators. He was very effort focused. It was always, "It's you, it's you."

He left the field feeling broken. He wondered what his life had really accomplished, and he ended up working as a construction supervisor for my uncle. As he got older, he came to see that it was never about his effort. By the time he died, he was a different person.

In 2009, when he was 81, my dad came back to the Philippines with my family. He ended up in the hospital with blood clots in both legs, at St. Luke's, the same hospital where I was born. And because of that interruption, he got to sit with some of the men he had discipled as teenagers forty years earlier, still serving God in their sixties. He wrote, "It humbled me, to realize anew that we sow, we water, but it's God that makes it grow."

On that same trip he wrote about what he called "a faulty ministry model" that had been part of his DNA, the idea that you have to aggressively make it happen through strategies and programs. And he wrote about being drawn instead to the way Jesus simply went about doing good. He ended it with three words: "He is enough!"

But even then, he didn't see all of it. When I was three years old, my mom and dad were discipling two young men in our home. One of them is the director of our school today. The other is the pastor of the church. They have been foundational to this ministry for about twenty years.

My dad thought it came to nothing. God wasn't done.

keyPoints: Slide up, silence
Maybe you came here broken
Church, marriage, money, your own heart
Feels like your work came to nothing
Not the end, maybe the beginning
"In the ministry of love, only the wounded can serve."
🔑 "God cannot use someone who is not broken. If you are, you're exactly where He wants you to be."
points.script:
So let me ask you.

Are you broken?

(Pause. Let it sit.)

Maybe you came to this conference broken. Maybe it's your church, or your marriage, or your finances, or your own heart. Maybe, like my dad, you feel like your work has come to nothing.

My dad quoted someone who said, "In the ministry of love, only the wounded can serve."

God cannot use someone who is not broken. If you are, you're exactly where He wants you to be.

That isn't the end of your ministry. It may be the beginning of it.

points.slide: We don't make them. His power makes them in our weakness.
keyPoints: Kintsugi: broken bowl repaired with gold
Worth more than before it broke
The cracks are where the gold is
Treasure in jars of clay
🔁 Character, calling, conviction. We don't make them. His power makes them in our weakness.

verses.text: But we have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this all-surpassing power is from God and not from us.

points.script:
In Japan there's an art called kintsugi. When a bowl breaks, they don't throw it away. They put it back together with gold. And the bowl becomes more valuable than it was before it broke. The cracks are where the gold is.

Paul says, "We have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this all-surpassing power is from God and not from us."

Character, calling, conviction. We don't make them. His power makes them in our weakness.

keyPoints: 2017: came to KIDS, ministry hurting
Damaged by past leadership
Money a struggle every month
Prayer: "Leadership, leadership, leadership"
Left business: lives impacted, not revenue
Came in like a CTO: plans, budgets, systems
My calling, delayed: Dad objected, went into business
Years of preparation; calling = who He makes you
"Christ in me," but lived like it was up to me
2019: healthier, still no leaders, tired

verses.text: Many are the plans in a person's heart, but it is the LORD's purpose that prevails.

points.script:
Let me tell you where I learned this. When I came to KIDS in 2017, the ministry was hurting. It had been damaged by past leadership. Every month was a struggle for money, and I prayed one prayer over and over: "Leadership, leadership, leadership."

I had left business because I was tired of measuring my life by how much revenue I created for a company. I wanted to measure my life by the lives I impact. But I brought my business habits with me. I came in like a CTO. Plans, budgets, fundraising, systems.

And it took me a long time to get here. I felt called to missions when I was young. My dad was actually the one who objected the most. I think he had been burnt by ministry, and he wanted his son to have a job and a foundation. So I went into business. For years I wondered why I didn't go sooner. Now I can see that those years were preparation. God wasn't wasting them. He had things to do in me first. Calling isn't just a job you get. It's someone He makes you into.

And I worked. I believed it was up to me to fix it. I would have told you it was Christ in me, but I lived like it was all up to me.

By 2019 the ministry was somewhat healthy. The finances were better. But the leaders I had prayed for still weren't there. And I was tired.

keyPoints: 2020: everything stopped
Shut in, two weeks of nothing
No money coming in, no plan
Couldn't fundraise or plan my way out
For the first time in a long time: nothing
points.script:
Then 2020 came, and everything stopped. We were shut in. For two weeks we did nothing. There was no money coming in, and I had no plan.

Everything I knew how to do didn't work. I couldn't fundraise my way out of it. I couldn't plan my way out of it. Everything I had been leaning on, my experience, my strength, my systems, was gone.

For the first time in a long time, I had nothing.

keyPoints: Hungry families at our gate
Cooking at the market
Local government asked for food
"Can we also feed the pastors?"
3,000 → 250,000 meals a week
Pastora Grace: more afraid of hunger than COVID
Didn't plan it; couldn't afford it
Birthed youth + family ministry, clinic ×10, 1,000+ pastors
points.script:
Then hungry families started coming to us, asking for food. So we started cooking and handing out meals at the market. Then the local government came and asked us for food, and I asked, "Can we also feed the pastors?"

One of our pastors, Pastora Grace, said it this way: "We are not afraid of COVID-19. We are more afraid of people dying because of hunger."

We went from about 3,000 meals a week to about 250,000 meals a week. I didn't plan that. Nobody would plan that. We didn't have the money for 3,000 meals, much less 250,000.

And out of that season came things we never could have built. A youth ministry. A family ministry. Our clinic grew about ten times. More than a thousand pastors connected with us through those feedings.

keyPoints: At the table: time to stop the feeding
Pastor Art: "We can't. There's people who are hungry, Norman."
"There's no money," walked away
Phone: former boss, not a Christian
His board: $50,000
"Never mind. The money came in."
Not my strength; God was already there
points.script:
One day we were sitting around a table, talking about stopping the feeding. There was no money. Pastor Art looked at me and said, "We can't. There's people who are hungry, Norman."

I told him there was no money, and I got up and walked away from the table. I looked at my phone, and there was a message from my former boss. He is not a Christian. He said his board wanted to donate $50,000.

I walked back to the table and said, "Never mind. The money came in."

I didn't raise that money. I walked away from that table with nothing, and God was already there. And we have so many stories from that season just like that one.

points.slideTitle: When I strive in my strength, I burn out.
points.slide: When I strive in His, I'm refreshed.
keyPoints: [@istnk2bm] The leaders came, the ones I prayed for
[@istn9rr6] Pastor Art: partner in the feedings
[@istnkahp] His son: Youth Lab, first youth ministry
[@istn02rf] Volunteers quarantined together → missionaries
[@istnchc5] 0 → 26 Filipino missionaries
[@istn7pjn] Hardest and most beautiful season
[@istnp7gg] Up at 4am, working till 10 or 11pm, loved it
[@istnkeil] Windsurfing: I don't make the wind
[@istnzvlx] Col 1:29: all His energy
[@istnvgp6] 🔑 "When I strive in my strength, I burn out. When I strive in His, I'm refreshed."

verses.text: To this end I strenuously contend with all the energy Christ so powerfully works in me.

points.script:
And then the leaders came, the ones I had been praying for. People we had never been connected to before. Pastor Art became my partner in the feedings. His son started Youth Lab, the first youth ministry we ever had. Volunteers who quarantined together at the ministry center caught a passion and became missionaries. We went from zero Filipino missionaries to twenty six. And they brought a whole new culture with them, a passion for prayer that we hadn't had before.

It was the hardest time of my life, and the most beautiful. I was up at four in the morning and working until ten or eleven at night, and I enjoyed every moment of it.

I used to windsurf. When you windsurf, you don't make the wind. You can't. You can pull on that sail as hard as you want, and if there's no wind, you go nowhere. But when the wind comes and you catch it, you fly. You're still working. Every muscle is working. But it doesn't drain you. It's the most fun you'll ever have.

That's what Paul means in Colossians 1:29: "To this end I strenuously contend with all the energy Christ so powerfully works in me." Paul is working hard. But the energy is Christ's.

When I strive in my strength, I burn out. When I strive in His, I'm refreshed.

points.slide: If I can do it myself, it isn't faith.
keyPoints: Building a high school, poor community
Still not finished: more floors, an auditorium
"How will you finish it?" I don't know
If I can see it on a spreadsheet, I need a calculator, not faith
"If God's love is extravagant, why not the school?"
🔑 "If I can do it myself, it isn't faith."

verses.text: Now faith is confidence in what we hope for and assurance about what we do not see.

points.script:
We are building a high school on land in a poor community, and it is still not finished. There are classrooms full of kids, and there are still more stories and an auditorium to go. People ask me how we are going to finish it. I don't know. When we first walked that land, I asked myself, if God's love is extravagant, why shouldn't the school be?

Hebrews says faith is confidence in what we hope for and assurance about what we do not see. If I can already see how it gets done, if the money is in the bank and the plan is on the spreadsheet, I don't need faith. I need a calculator.

I have learned this: if I can do it myself, it isn't faith.

keyPoints: (Optional, judgment call on the day)
A very personal season
My conviction about my life gave way
Not going into it
God used the loss to change me
points.script: (Optional, judgment call on the day.) There was also a season in my own life, a very personal one, where my own conviction about how my life would go simply gave way. I won't go into it today. But God used that loss to change me in ways my strength never could.

keyPoints: I'm not the strong one; I never was
Same pattern as Peter, as my dad
🔁 Character, calling, conviction. We don't make them. His power makes them in our weakness.

verses.text: Not only so, but we also glory in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance; perseverance, character; and character, hope.

points.script:
So that's what I learned. I'm not the strong one. I never was. It's the same pattern we saw in Peter, and in my dad. God let the strength run out, so He could be the strength.

Paul says suffering produces perseverance, and perseverance produces character. Character isn't something you build on a good day.

Character, calling, conviction. We don't make them. His power makes them in our weakness.

points.slide: Ministry is messy, and there's beauty in the mess.
keyPoints: CCC sound tidy: in a box, checked off
The opposite is true
Painter's palette: a mess
Every painting started on a messy palette
If life were straight lines, we wouldn't need God
God puts us where the mess shows up
🔑 "Ministry is messy, and there's beauty in the mess."
points.script:
Character, calling and conviction sound very tidy, don't they? Like something you could put in a box and check off. Character, check. Calling, check. Conviction, check.

The opposite is true.

Look at a painter's palette. It's a mess. Colors smeared everywhere, blobs, drips, brushes dipped in three colors at once. If all you ever saw was the palette, you'd say, what a mess. But somewhere behind it, there's a painting. Every beautiful painting started on a messy palette.

Ministry is messy, and there's beauty in the mess. If life were all straight lines, we wouldn't need God. And I've come to believe God intentionally puts us right where the mess shows up, so that He can be the one who makes it work.

keyPoints: Mess teaches humility
I'm not in control; I can't fix it
Expect clean → disappointed → angry
Dad: the small interruptions are harder than the big trials
Even now, strained relationships; God at work in the middle
Expect the mess, and God in it
points.script:
The mess teaches us humility. I'm not in control, and I can't fix it.

And if I expect it to be clean, I will be disappointed, and then I will be angry. Angry at my staff, angry at the board, angry at the pastors who didn't show up, and if I'm honest, angry at God.

My dad once said it's easier not to question God about the big trials than about the small daily interruptions. The big things, we give to God. It's the little things that get under our skin.

Even right now, there are relationships in our ministry that are strained. It's messy. And I am seeing God at work everywhere in the middle of it.

So expect the mess. And expect God in it.

points.slide: I find God's voice in the doing, not just the waiting.
keyPoints: Blackaby: find where God is working, join Him
Jesus: "My Father is always at work"
Not my best place: sitting still for hours
Try something, see if God blesses it
Adjust, or move on
Hungry family, a pastor, a volunteer who won't go home
Whole life becomes my prayer life
"Where God goes, go there. Don't expect God to follow us."
🔑 "I find God's voice in the doing, not just the waiting."

verses.text: In his defense Jesus said to them, "My Father is always at his work to this very day, and I too am working." ... Jesus gave them this answer: "Very truly I tell you, the Son can do nothing by himself; he can do only what he sees his Father doing, because whatever the Father does the Son also does."

points.script:
Henry Blackaby taught us to find where God is working and join Him. Jesus said, "My Father is always at his work to this very day, and I too am working." And, "The Son can do nothing by himself; he can do only what he sees his Father doing."

I'll be honest. Sitting still for hours is not where I hear God best. I've tried. For me, I find God's voice in the doing, not just the waiting.

I try something, I see if God blesses it, and I adjust or I move on. A hungry family at the gate. A pastor who needs food. A volunteer who doesn't want to go home. That's where the Father is working, and I join Him. COVID taught me that. Where God goes, go there. Don't expect God to follow us. Sometimes a disaster is the biggest opportunity He gives you.

My whole life becomes my prayer life.

keyPoints: Balance: don't go looking for mess
Don't create it
Bring God's order into it
Christ didn't stand outside our mess
"The Word became flesh"
Born in a feeding trough, in a barn
God's answer to the mess: a baby in a manger
Tondo 2009: Grace, Lola Maming's mangoes
"Probably the only Jesus many had ever seen"

verses.text: The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth.

points.script:
Now, that doesn't mean we go looking for mess, or that we create it. Some of us are very good at creating it. We bring God's order into it.

That's what Christ did. He didn't stand outside our mess and tell us to clean it up. He came down into the middle of it. "The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us."

He was born in a barn and laid in a feeding trough, with the animals. That is about as messy as it gets. God's answer to our mess wasn't a memo. It was a baby in a manger.

In 2009, my wife Tina and I were in Tondo, and we handed a bag of groceries to a woman named Grace. She worked the streets. She came to the Bible study under the bridge, and on the second day she wept, overwhelmed by how much Jesus loved her. Then an old woman who sells mangoes, Lola Maming, brought us a kilo of mangoes she couldn't afford to give. We took them so she could give. And then we found out Lola Maming was Grace's aunt. My dad wrote, "We were probably the only Jesus many of them had ever seen." That's what it looks like to bring His order into the mess. You go in.

points.slideTitle: God doesn't see a point in time.
keyPoints: In the middle of the mess, remember:
Dad's circus story: knothole vs. up in the tree
"God sees at one glance every episode of our lives"
Don't judge your ministry, or anyone else, by one frame
He who began a good work will finish it
🔑 "God doesn't see a point in time. He sees the whole journey."

verses.text: being confident of this, that he who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus.

points.script:
And when you are in the middle of the mess, remember this.

My dad used to tell a story about two boys at the circus. One watches through a knothole in the fence, and he sees one animal at a time going by. The other boy is up in a tree, and he sees the whole circus at one glance. My dad said, "God sees at one glance every episode of our lives."

So don't judge your ministry by one frame. And don't judge anyone else's by one frame either. He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion.

God doesn't see a point in time. He sees the whole journey.

points.slide: We don't make them. His power makes them in the mess.
keyPoints: Paul's best letters: from prison
Philippians: joy, from a cell
"It is God who works in you" (Phil 2:13)
🔁 Character, calling, conviction. We don't make them. His power makes them in the mess.

verses.text: for it is God who works in you to will and to act in order to fulfill his good purpose.

points.script:
Remember, Paul wrote some of his most beautiful letters from prison. Philippians, the letter about joy, was written in chains. The mess didn't stop what God was doing in him. The mess was where God was doing it. And in that same letter he writes, "It is God who works in you to will and to act in order to fulfill his good purpose." From a prison cell.

Character, calling, conviction. We don't make them. His power makes them in the mess.

keyPoints: Callback: "Don't expect it to look any different"
Don't expect the mess to be different either
The power and the mess: the same thing
points.script:
At the beginning I told you not to expect His power to look any different for you than it did for the disciples. Don't expect the mess to be any different either.

The power and the mess aren't two different things. They're the same thing.

If you go home from this conference and things get hard, don't think the power left you. That may be the very moment it's working. Peter by the fire. My dad in that hospital bed. Me at that table with no money. The mess is not a sign that God left.

points.slide: The mess is where the power lives.
keyPoints: Started in a manger, ended at a cross
Cross: biggest mess in history
And the greatest display of His power
Foolishness to some; to us, the power of God
🔑 "The mess is where the power lives."

verses.text: For the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God. ... For the foolishness of God is wiser than human wisdom, and the weakness of God is stronger than human strength.

points.script:
Because the mess is where the power lives.

It started in a manger, and it went all the way to a cross. Think about the cross. From the outside, it was the biggest mess in all of history. The Son of God, beaten, mocked, hanging between two criminals, His friends gone. And it was the greatest display of God's power the world has ever seen.

Paul says, "The message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God." The weakness of God is stronger than human strength.

points.slideTitle: There's a thin line between faith and insanity.
keyPoints: High school: people thought I was crazy
Sometimes I did too
From outside, faith and insanity look the same
Never near the line → never need faith
🔑 "There's a thin line between faith and insanity. Walk the line."
points.script:
When we started building the high school, people thought I was crazy. Some days I thought I was crazy too.

From the outside, faith and insanity can look exactly the same. And if you never go anywhere near that line, you will never need faith. Walking the line doesn't mean doing something foolish. It means doing the next thing He shows you, even when you can't see how it ends.

There's a thin line between faith and insanity. Walk the line.

keyPoints: Came to talk about nothing after all
Remember the branch
Apart from Him, nothing. In Him, fruit.
Not bad news: it was never up to you

verses.text: For we are God's handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance for us to do.

points.script:
It turns out I came to talk about nothing after all.

Remember the branch. Apart from Him, nothing. In Him, fruit.

And that isn't bad news. It's the best news I know. It means it was never up to you. We are His handiwork, created in Christ Jesus for good works He prepared in advance. He's the one doing the making.

So as you go into the next three sessions, as we go deep on character, and on calling, and on conviction, I want you to remember where they come from.

points.slide: Listen for what He's making you into.
keyPoints: Read the closing paragraph
Kingdom → power → made them different
Peter's conviction failed by a fire
God formed, clarified, planted: His
"Don't listen for what you need to do for God"
"Listen for what He's making you into"
Hand off to the next three speakers
points.script: The disciples asked for a kingdom, and Jesus gave them power. But it didn't make life easier. It made them different. Peter had his own conviction: "I will never deny you." And it failed him by a fire, in front of a servant girl. Then, through prison, persecution and failure, God did what Peter never could. He formed a character that was His, made clear a calling that was His, and planted a conviction that was His. It still works that way. So over the next three sessions, don't listen for what you need to do for God. Listen for what He's making you into.
